# Sources: behavioural science behind outreach messages

Read status: **full** (the paper or its full text page was read, at least the method and results), **part** (the
paper was read in part, for the stated figures), **summary** (only an abstract, a database record, press coverage
or a secondary write-up was read). Everything was read on 2026-10-29.

## Replication and publication bias

| Source | URL | Read | One line |
|---|---|---|---|
| DellaVigna and Linos 2022, Econometrica 90(1) | https://www.econometricsociety.org/publications/econometrica/2022/01/01/rcts-scale-comprehensive-evidence-two-nudge-units | summary | 126 nudge unit trials, 23M people: 1.4 points (8.0%) against 8.7 points (33.4%) in journals; about 70% of the gap is selective publication |
| NBER working paper w27594 (same) | https://nber.org/papers/w27594 | summary | Source of the 8.7 point academic figure |
| Maier et al. 2022, PNAS letter | https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9351501/ | summary | After a publication bias correction, no overall evidence for nudges in Mertens et al.'s meta-analysis |
| Maier et al. rejoinder | https://www.bayesianspectacles.org/rejoinder-no-evidence-for-nudging/ | summary | Title kept; authors say with hindsight they would have written "no overall evidence"; after correction only 21.5% of effects above d = 0.3 |
